import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepClassifyZar
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeAtlasFactor
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarVehicle

/-!
# Conditional assembly kit for affine divisor representability

This file isolates the formal tail between a chart-wise universal certified family and
the affine equivalence of DDR-9.F6.  It deliberately makes the remaining F5 hypotheses
explicit:

* `divRepPullAt` pulls a supplied chart family along a map out of a carve-chart ring;
* `DivRepChartFamily.IsCompatible` is the exact choice-independence statement needed to
  glue those local pullbacks;
* `DivRepAffinePullback` packages the output of that glue together with the two laws and
  naturality;
* `DivRepAffinePullback.equiv` turns those data into the affine equivalence, using the
  already-landed uniqueness theorem for `divRepClassifyZar` for the hom-side law.

No universal family, compatibility, inverse law, or representability theorem is asserted
here.  The future F5 construction must supply the fields of these interfaces.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option quotPrecheck false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open Grassmannian Scheme

section Curve

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]

noncomputable local instance instOverCleftDivRepAffKit :
    C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩

variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [IsIntegral C.left]
  [LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [IsDominant pi]
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
variable [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0)]
  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)]
variable (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
variable (g : ℕ)
variable (hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1)
variable (hchi : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
variable (r1 r2 : ℕ)
variable (b1 : Module.Basis (Fin r1) k
  ↥(divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
variable (b2 : Module.Basis (Fin r2) k
  ↥(divisorSections k
    ((windowM_choice pi hpi g + windowS_choice pi hpi g) • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))

local notation "DivOver" =>
  divSchemeOver k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm)

local notation "ChartRing" => fun i j =>
  DivCarveChartRing k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm) i j

local notation "ChartMap" => fun i j =>
  divCarveChartToDivScheme k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm) i j

/-! ## F5: pullback from one supplied universal chart family -/

/-- Pull a supplied certified family on one carve chart to a test algebra and pass to
the locally certified quotient.  This is the choice-free per-chart operation from which
F5's affine forward map is glued. -/
noncomputable def divRepPullAt
    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
      CertifiedDivisorFamily C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) : DivFamZar C S pi g :=
  DivFamZar.mapAlgHom omega (DivFam.mk (U i j)).toZar

set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
@[simp]
theorem divRepPullAt_id
    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
      CertifiedDivisorFamily C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J) :
    divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j (AlgHom.id k (ChartRing i j))
      = (DivFam.mk (U i j)).toZar :=
  DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_id _

set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
/-- Pulling a chart family through two algebra maps is the same as pulling it through
their composite.  This is the algebraic part of F5 naturality. -/
theorem divRepPullAt_comp
    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
      CertifiedDivisorFamily C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
    {S T : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [CommRing T] [Algebra k T]
    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (phi : S →ₐ[k] T) :
    DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi (divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega)
      = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j (phi.comp omega) :=
  (DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp omega phi (DivFam.mk (U i j)).toZar).symm

namespace DivRepChartFamily

/-- The precise F5 overlap obligation for a supplied family on every carve chart:
two chart points inducing the same morphism to `DivScheme` have equal pulled locally
certified divisor classes.  The future universal-family construction proves this from
its epsilon identity and the total mono theorem. -/
def IsCompatible
    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
      CertifiedDivisorFamily C (ChartRing i j) pi g) : Prop :=
  ∀ {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
    (i' : (glueData k g r1).J) (j' : (glueData k g r2).J)
    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (omega' : ChartRing i' j' →ₐ[k] S),
    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i j
        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega'.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i' j' →
      divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega
        = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i' j' omega'

set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
/-- Compatibility may be applied when both chart presentations are identified with a
common morphism.  This is the form used on overlaps of an atlas factorization. -/
theorem pullAt_eq_of_eq_common
    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
      CertifiedDivisorFamily C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
    (hU : IsCompatible (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U)
    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
    (i' : (glueData k g r1).J) (j' : (glueData k g r2).J)
    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (omega' : ChartRing i' j' →ₐ[k] S)
    (q : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶
      DivScheme k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
        (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
        (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm))
    (homega : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i j = q)
    (homega' : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega'.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i' j' = q) :
    divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega
      = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i' j' omega' :=
  hU i j i' j' omega omega' (homega.trans homega'.symm)

end DivRepChartFamily

/-! ## F6: package a completed affine pullback as an equivalence -/

/-- The exact output expected from F5 before the affine equivalence is packaged.
`isDivRepClassify_pull` is the hom-side law in the refinement-stable clause spelling;
classifier uniqueness turns it into the second inverse law automatically. -/
structure DivRepAffinePullback where
  pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S],
    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) → DivFamZar C S pi g
  pull_classify : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (F : DivFamZar C S pi g),
    pull S (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F) = F
  isDivRepClassify_pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver),
    IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 (pull S v) v.left
  pull_naturality : ∀ {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (phi : A →ₐ[k] B) (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver),
    pull B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v) = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi (pull A v)

namespace DivRepAffinePullback

/-- The affine representability equivalence assembled from an F5 pullback package.
The inverse is the landed backward classifier; its hom-side inverse law follows from
`divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify`. -/
noncomputable def equiv
    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] :
    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) ≃ DivFamZar C S pi g where
  toFun := D.pull S
  invFun := divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S
  left_inv v :=
    (divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
      (D.pull S v) v (D.isDivRepClassify_pull S v)).symm
  right_inv := D.pull_classify S

@[simp]
theorem equiv_apply
    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) :
    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S v = D.pull S v :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem equiv_symm_apply
    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (F : DivFamZar C S pi g) :
    (equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)

/-! ## The reusable finiteness core -/

/-- **The `S`-span of the range of an `R`-linear map out of a finite `R`-module is `S`-finite.**
For an `R`-algebra `S`, a finite `R`-module `M`, and a scalar-tower `S`-module `N`, the
`S`-submodule `Submodule.span S (Set.range f)` generated by the image of `f : M →ₗ[R] N` is a
finite `S`-module: a finite `R`-generating set `T` of `M` yields the finite `S`-generating set
`f '' T` (every `f m` is an `R`-combination of the `f tᵢ`, hence an `S`-combination).  Pure
algebra; the finiteness route for the concrete colength `N z`. -/
theorem Module.Finite.span_range_of_finite_isScalarTower
    {R S M N : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module S N] [IsScalarTower R S N]
    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) :
    Module.Finite S (Submodule.span S (Set.range f)) := by
  obtain ⟨T, hT⟩ := (Module.Finite.fg_top (R := R) (M := M))
  have hspan : Submodule.span S (Set.range f) = Submodule.span S (f '' T) := by
    apply le_antisymm
    · rw [Submodule.span_le]
      rintro _ ⟨m, rfl⟩
      have hm : m ∈ Submodule.span R (T : Set M) := by rw [hT]; trivial
      have hfm : f m ∈ Submodule.span R (f '' T) := by
        rw [← Submodule.map_span]
        exact Submodule.mem_map_of_mem hm
      exact (Submodule.span_le_restrictScalars R S (f '' T)) hfm
    · exact Submodule.span_mono (Set.image_subset_range f T)
  rw [hspan]
  exact Module.Finite.iff_fg.mpr (Submodule.fg_span (T.finite_toSet.image f))

/-! ## The concrete chart-level colength `N z` -/

/-- **The concrete chart-level colength `N z`** (I-0302 §residual 2a): the `Γ(V)`-submodule of
the colength ring `Γ(V) ⧸ ⟨read s⟩` generated by the chart readings `read ψ` of the submodule

noncomputable def chartColengthModule (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool)
    (s : relThetaSections C R π a) :
    Submodule Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)
      (Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b) ⧸
        Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) s}) :=
  Submodule.span _ (Set.range
    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) s})).toLinearMap.comp
      (chartReadMap K b)))

    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool)

    Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) s})
        (relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) ψ) ∈ chartColengthModule K b s :=
  Submodule.subset_span ⟨⟨ψ, hψ⟩, rfl⟩

finite `R`-module (the chart readings of a finite generating set of `K` span `N z`). -/

theorem forall_mul_read_mem_span_of_forall_smul_eq_zero
    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool)

      rw [Algebra.smul_def, Ideal.Quotient.algebraMap_eq, ← map_mul]] at hz'

## §2 — Gap (b): the achiever does NOT cut `d_p` globally (rigorous degree bookkeeping)

### The setup (all landed)

* The window `T := divUniversalFibreKM C … κ(p)` **equals the complete linear system**
  `H⁰(N − d_p)`:

### The achiever pins order at `z` ONLY

The achiever `Scheme.exists_coeffAt_eq_baseDivisorAt` (`RiemannRoch/BaseDivisor.lean:143`)
is a **per‑point `sInf` witness**: `Nat.sInf_mem` (line 149) picks a nonzero `f ∈ T` that

`exists_relThetaWindowEquiv_…_achieves_seedPrime`) is exactly this at `A = N − d_p` and the

```
coeffAt hz ((N − d_p) + div(read sec z)) = baseDivisorAt(T, N − d_p, z).
```

### The degree count forcing an extra zero

Let `f := read sec z ∈ T = H⁰(N − d_p)`, `f ≠ 0`. Then
`E := (N − d_p) + div f ≥ 0` (effective, membership in `H⁰`), and
```
deg E = deg(N − d_p) + deg(div f) = (deg N − g) + 0 = deg N − g ≥ 2 > 0
```
(principal divisor has degree 0; `deg d_p = g`). So **`f` has `deg N − g ≥ 2` zeros
(with multiplicity), recorded by `E`, on the κ(p)‑fibre.** The achiever fixes only `E_z`.

**Global fibre divisibility** — the thing the 2c bridge / germ / flat lemmas all need — is
`read ψ ∈ ⟨read sec z⟩` for every `ψ`, over the whole κ(p)‑fibre chart. As sections this
is `div f ≤ div(read ψ)` for all `ψ`, i.e.
```
E = (N − d_p) + div f  ≤  (N − d_p) + div(read ψ) =: E_ψ   for every ψ,
```
i.e. `E ≤ inf_ψ E_ψ = baseDivisor(T, N − d_p) =: B` (the fixed/base part of the system).

**This is impossible for `dim T ≥ 2`.** Suppose it held; then `E ≤ B ≤ E` (as `B` is a
lower bound and `E` is one member's divisor `≥ B` too, forcing `E = B`), so the single
member `f` achieves the base divisor *at every point*. Then `B = E` has degree `deg N − g`,
the moving part `N − d_p − B` has degree `(deg N − g) − (deg N − g) = 0`, and
`T = H⁰(N − d_p) = H⁰((N − d_p − B) + B) ≅ H⁰(N − d_p − B)` has `dim = h⁰(deg‑0 divisor) = 1`
(only constants on the fibre curve). This **contradicts `dim T = deg N + 1 − 2g ≥ 2`**.

Therefore there is a zero `w ≠ z` of `f` with `E_w > B_w = min_ψ E_{ψ,w}`, i.e. the achiever
*at `w`* (a **different** section `f_w`, BaseDivisor:143 at `x = w`) has
`div(f_w)_w < div(f)_w`, so `read sec z = f` does **not** divide `read f_w` at `w`.

> **Answer to the crux question: does `read sec z` cut `d_p` GLOBALLY by degree count?
> NO.** The degree count `deg E = deg N − g ≥ 2 > 0` combined with `dim T ≥ 2` *forces*
> genuine extra zeros of `read sec z` away from `z`, at which other readings have strictly
> smaller order. `⟨read sec z⟩ ⊊` the divisor ideal over the fibre; global divisibility
> FAILS. This is exactly I‑0288's wall (facts 1 + 3), now nailed with the closed degree
> identity. The achiever cuts `d_p` at `z` and nowhere else.

Option (ii) — "does flat + carve rank‑g (`hsub_chart`, fibre‑injectivity) give it?": **no.**
`hsub_chart` is fibre *injectivity* (the reading map's rank / the quotient's flatness). It
transports/lifts *existing* fibre facts; it cannot upgrade single‑point achievement to a
whole‑fibre common divisor. The flat's advertised role (I‑0302 §2b: "lift base‑fibre
generation over κ(p) to the curve‑point fibre κ(z)") is **backwards** — it needs κ(p)
generation as *input*, which is precisely the false global statement. Flatness runs
κ(p) ⟹ (finer), never the reverse.

   219	    Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k M)))
   220	      ≅ Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap L M)))

   222	  eqToIso (by rw [show Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k M))

   224	          ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)) by
   225	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq]]) ≪≫

   229	(`eqToIso rfl`), composed with the op of the `Over.mapComp` reassociation. -/

   232	        ⋙ (Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))).op
   233	      ≅ (Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k M)))).op :=
   234	  eqToIso rfl ≪≫ (NatIso.op (σMapCompIso k L M))

   237	`baseChange.compIso` vehicle. -/

   240	      ≅ (Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k M)))).op ⋙ pic0Functor C :=
   241	  eCurve k L M C

   243	    ≪≫ Functor.isoWhiskerLeft
   244	        (Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap L M)))).op (pic0Theta k L C)
   245	    ≪≫ (Functor.associator _ _ _).symm
   246	    ≪≫ Functor.isoWhiskerRight (αOp k L M) (pic0Functor C)

name: horizon
description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`. Live state is under `.archon-horizon/`
and the manifest is `config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how agents talk across sessions (and projects). Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Inbox commands warn when the open working set—especially
  `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a `"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body …`
at each significant step. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

## Do the work (Lean)

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
mathlib — query it:

| You want | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |

`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
back to grep.

Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.

- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.

## Read the other projects

They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.

## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)

Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain

.archon-horizon/runs/0039/sessions/0001-horizon-interactive/transcript.jsonl-76-{"kind": "tool_result", "at": "2026-07-18T07:14:16.154982+00:00", "text": "", "tool": "", "data": {"content": "1	# Concurrent-lane protocol (2026-07-16, from inbox I-0149's incidents — BINDING for parallel agent fleets)
2	
3	Adopted after the 2026-07-16 evening wave's four incidents (I-0149). These rules extend the
4	standing handoff protocol (07-14/14b/15) for any session running two or more lanes in this
5	workspace.
6	
7	## 1. Ledger commits: private index + compare-and-swap (the shared-index race)
8	
9	All lanes commit through one `workspace.git`; concurrent `git add`+`commit` through the
10	SHARED index can interleave and record spurious deletions of another lane's
11	freshly-committed files (happened in `6197c9676`, 862 lines vanished from HEAD, restored
12	byte-identical in `a640fef5b`). Concurrent lanes MUST commit via a private index:
13	
14	```bash
15	cd /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
16	GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git
17	export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)
18	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. read-tree HEAD
19	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. add <ONLY your paths…>
20	TREE=$(git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. write-tree)
21	PARENT=$(git --git-dir=$GD rev-parse HEAD)
22	COMMIT=$(git --git-dir=$GD -c user.name="Archon Horizon" -c user.email="archon-horizon@local" \
23	  commit-tree $TREE -p $PARENT -m "<math-first message>
24	
25	Archon-Commit: agent
26	Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>")
27	git --git-dir=$GD update-ref refs/heads/main $COMMIT $PARENT   # CAS: fails if HEAD moved
28	unset GIT_INDEX_FILE
29	```
30	
31	If the `update-ref` CAS fails (HEAD moved), re-read HEAD and repeat — never force.
32	ALWAYS verify afterward: `git --git-dir=$GD show --stat HEAD` must touch only your paths.
33	A single-lane session may keep the plain `add`+`commit` recipe, but must still verify.
34	
35	## 2. The lake mutex is a mkdir DIRECTORY lock — never flock a file there
36	
37	`/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock` is acquired by `mkdir` (atomic; a crash leaves a
38	directory that the next holder's timeout logic can reap). It is NOT a flock file: a lane
39	that runs `flock /tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock …` creates a plain FILE at the
40	path, and every mkdir-acquire loop then spins forever (this deadlocked all lanes
41	15:18–19:10 on 2026-07-16 until a human deleted it). Acquire pattern:
42	
43	```bash
44	LOCK=/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock
45	while ! mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; do
46	  if [ -f "$LOCK" ]; then echo "STALE: plain file at $LOCK (protocol violation) — remove it" >&2; break; fi
47	  sleep 10
48	done
49	# … lake build … ; rmdir "$LOCK"
50	```
51	
52	A plain FILE at the lock path is by definition stale (mkdir creates directories) — detect
53	it immediately, report, and remove; do not wait on it.
54	
55	## 3. /tmp quota with >3 lanes
56	
57	uid-1001 tmpfs quota exhaustion (EDQUOT) bricked every Bash call machine-wide
58	(~19:00–19:20). With more than ~3 concurrent lanes, keep scratch artifacts small, clean up
59	build temp dirs, and if Bash starts failing with quota errors, stop and report rather than
60	retry-looping.
61	
62	## 4. The root import file: commit only your own lines (I-0153)
63	
64	`AlgebraicJacobian.lean` is edited by every lane. Committing the WHOLE file via any recipe
65	sweeps siblings' uncommitted import lines into HEAD — the root then references files not yet
66	in HEAD (red for fresh checkouts), and a later sibling's whole-file commit can sweep or drop
67	YOUR line the same way. Before committing the root file: run
68	`git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD -- <project>/AlgebraicJacobian.lean` — if lines
69	other than yours differ, either (a) verify every swept import's file is already committed in
70	HEAD and say so in the commit message, or (b) construct the commit from HEAD's version plus
71	only your lines (apply a minimal patch to a temp checkout of the HEAD blob). Never commit a
72	root file that references uncommitted files without naming that in the message.
73	
74	## 5. The AJCR mutex is for AJCR lake invocations only
75	
76	No cross-workspace use (an OpenGA-Horizon agent squatted it ~25 min for its own
77	`lake cache get`, silently serializing AJCR lanes against unrelated work). Other
78	workspaces must use their own lock paths.

90	## 1. ADJUDICATION A — the dictionary consumption and the off-overlap question (I-0186 item 2 × I-0182)
91	
92	**Question.** Does DD-R consume the one-sided field dictionary {backward map `hsurj` +
93	`divFamDivisor_injective`} with P-fib's divisor normalized off the chart overlap
94	`π⁻¹(Gm)`, or must the general-MV `hdeg` brick be funded?
95	
96	**Verdict: NEITHER. (i) The off-overlap normalization is mathematically unavailable,
97	and (ii) DD-R consumes neither `hsurj` nor `hdeg` — the universal-family architecture
98	replaces the dictionary consumption entirely.** The I-0182 one-sided-dictionary route
99	is hereby SUPERSEDED for DD-R (it remains correct as a statement about the field
100	dictionary; its consumer is DAT-B, see the boundary flag below).
101	
102	**(i) Evidence that off-overlap support cannot be arranged.** P-fib's `D` is the
103	modulus itself, not an auxiliary choice: in `existsUnique_effective_divisor_of_carve`
104	(`PFib.lean:241`) the divisor is *defined* as `D := Scheme.baseDivisor K KM (M•F)`
105	(`PFib.lean:282`) — the base divisor of the *given* window — and the uniqueness clause
106	pins it pointwise by `baseDivisorAt_normalization` (`:127`): the F1 "normalization"
107	normalizes the *window relative to `D`* (no residual base point), never `D`'s support.
108	As the carve point varies over `Z(♦)`, `D` ranges over **every** effective degree-`g`
109	divisor — the ⟸ direction (DD-4 §2.3) embeds `g·x` for every closed `x`, including
110	`x ∈ π⁻¹(Gm)` = the nonempty chart overlap (`relCover`/`pullbackProd`,
111	`RelativeTwoCover.lean:128`; nonemptiness per I-0186). There is no translation (the
112	curve has no group structure) and no rescale (unit rescaling of `K_M` fixes `bd`).
113	I-0186 item 2 is answered: **NO — P-fib's divisor cannot be arranged off-overlap.**
114	
115	**(ii) Why DD-R nevertheless needs no dictionary.** DD-R's backward direction is
116	*pullback of a universal certified family* constructed over `Z(♦)`'s charts by local
117	generators from the universal carve pair (worksheet §3.4.1) — the equations are window
118	*achievers*, never `pointEquations` products; `divFamOfDivisor` appears nowhere. The
119	only degree identity DD-R needs is fibrewise, **for carve-certified families only**,
120	and it closes without Mayer–Vietoris by the **certified-degree pinch** (DDR-2 below):
121	at a field point, `K_M = H⁰(MF − D_F)` (the sections dictionary, DD-4 Task 5's field
122	content) with corank `g` in `H_M`; the section bound
123	(`h0_divisorSheaf_le_max_of_h0_one`, SectionBound:248) forces `deg D_F ≤ 2g` (the F1
124	move, exactly as `PFib.lean:294–303`); then the exact normalization window
125	(`rank_normalization`, WindowLedger:396, licensed at `deg ≤ 2g` by
126	`two_mul_genus_le_M_mul_windowδ`, WindowLedgerF3:102) gives
127	`r_M − g = h⁰(MF − D_F) = Mδ − deg D_F + 1 − g`, i.e. `deg D_F = g`. No adaptation
128	independence, no inclusion–exclusion, no `hdeg`. I-0179's wall is not touched.
129	
130	**The EXACT hypotheses DD-R's bricks carry**: `adaptation.IsCertified g` plus carve
131	membership (the pair `ε(F)` satisfies `(♦)`, corank exactly `g`) — never a support
132	condition `supp D ∩ π⁻¹(Gm) = ∅`, never `hdeg`, never `hsurj`. Any DD-R prover writing

    12	/-!
    13	# The two-coordinate recurrence in a field window
    14	
    15	For `F = fiberWeilDivisor pi` and `u = fiberCoordUnit pi`, the two sections
    16	`1` and `u⁻¹` of `O(F)` generate every sufficiently large window:
    17	
    18	`H⁰(O((m + 1)F)) = H⁰(O(mF)) + u⁻¹ H⁰(O(mF))`.
    19	
    20	The proof is the divisor-section form of the standard two-chart argument.  The
    21	two shifted divisors are `mF` and `mF - div(u⁻¹)`; their supremum is
    22	`(m + 1)F`, while the degree of their infimum is `(m - 1) deg(F)`.  Thus the
    23	four `H¹` hypotheses needed by `divisorSections_sup` are discharged by the
    24	window ledger as soon as `windowS ≤ m`.
    25	
    26	The final pair theorem records the same recurrence through the existing field
    27	theta presentation `thetaSectionPair`.  It is intentionally stated over a
    28	field curve; residue-field specialisations can instantiate it without any
    29	relative nilpotent-base assertion.
    30	-/

    71	private lemma coeffAt_nsmul (n : Nat) (D : C.left.CurveDivisor) {x : C.left}
    72	    (hx : x ≠ genericPoint C.left) :
    73	    coeffAt hx (n • D) = (n : Int) * coeffAt hx D := by
    74	  induction n with
    75	  | zero => simp
    76	  | succ n ih =>
    77	      rw [succ_nsmul, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, ih, Nat.cast_succ]
    78	      ring

    80	private lemma coeffAt_divOf_inv (v : C.left.functionFieldˣ) {x : C.left}
    81	    (hx : x ≠ genericPoint C.left) :
    82	    coeffAt hx (Scheme.divOf (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) v⁻¹) =
    83	      -coeffAt hx (Scheme.divOf (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) v) := by
    84	  have h : Scheme.divOf (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) v⁻¹ +
    85	      Scheme.divOf (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) v = 0 := by
    86	    rw [← Scheme.divOf_mul, inv_mul_cancel, Scheme.divOf_one]
    87	  have hc := congrArg (coeffAt hx) h
    88	  rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero] at hc
    89	  linarith

    94	noncomputable def thetaCoordinateFstOne
    95	    (_hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) : H 1 :=
    96	  ⟨1, by
    97	    simpa only [one_smul] using
    98	      (one_mem_divisorSections_top k (fiberWeilDivisor_nonneg pi))⟩

   100	private theorem fiberCoordUnit_inv_mem_divisorSections :
   101	    (((u⁻¹ : C.left.functionFieldˣ) : C.left.functionField)) ∈
   102	      divisorSections k (1 • F) ⊤ := by
   103	  let v : C.left.functionFieldˣ := u⁻¹
   104	  change (v : C.left.functionField) ∈ divisorSections k (1 • F) ⊤
   105	  rw [mem_divisorSections_top_iff k (Units.ne_zero v)]
   106	  refine CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mpr (fun x hx => ?_)
   107	  have hmk : Units.mk0 (v : C.left.functionField) (Units.ne_zero v) = v :=
   108	    Units.ext rfl
   109	  rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero, hmk, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, coeffAt_nsmul,
   110	    fiberWeilDivisor_coeffAt pi, coeffAt_divOf_inv]
   111	  have hleft : coeffAt hx
   112	      (Scheme.divOf (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) u) ≤
   113	      max (coeffAt hx (Scheme.divOf
   114	        (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) u)) 0 := le_max_left _ _
   115	  norm_num

   135	/-! ## Divisor arithmetic behind the recurrence -/
   136	
   137	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
   138	-- The coefficientwise max/subtraction normalization is nonlinear in the order value.
   139	theorem thetaCoordinate_sup (m : Nat) :
   140	    (m • F) ⊔ thetaCoordinateSndDivisor (C := C) pi m = (1 + m) • F := by
   141	  refine CurveDivisor.ext_coeffAt (fun x hx => ?_)
   142	  rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_sup, thetaCoordinateSndDivisor,
   143	    CurveDivisor.coeffAt_sub]
   144	  simp only [coeffAt_nsmul, fiberWeilDivisor_coeffAt, coeffAt_divOf_inv]
   145	  by_cases hd : coeffAt hx (Scheme.divOf (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) u) ≤ 0
   146	  · have hmax : max (coeffAt hx (Scheme.divOf
   147	        (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) u)) 0 = 0 := max_eq_right hd
   148	    simp only [hmax]
   149	    have hcomp : (m : Int) * 0 - -coeffAt hx
   150	        (Scheme.divOf (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) u) ≤ (m : Int) * 0 := by
   151	      simpa using hd
   152	    rw [max_eq_left hcomp]
   153	    norm_num
   154	  · have hd' : 0 ≤ coeffAt hx
   155	        (Scheme.divOf (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) u) :=
   156	      le_of_lt (lt_of_not_ge hd)
   157	    have hmax : max (coeffAt hx (Scheme.divOf
   158	        (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) u)) 0 =
   159	        coeffAt hx (Scheme.divOf (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) u) :=
   160	      max_eq_left hd'
   161	    simp only [hmax]
   162	    have hcomp : (m : Int) * coeffAt hx
   163	          (Scheme.divOf (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) u) ≤
   164	        (m : Int) * coeffAt hx
   165	          (Scheme.divOf (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) u) - -
   166	          coeffAt hx (Scheme.divOf (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) u) := by
   167	      nlinarith [Int.natCast_nonneg m, hd']
   168	    rw [max_eq_right hcomp]
   169	    push_cast
   170	    ring

   172	theorem thetaCoordinateSndDivisor_deg (m : Nat) :
   173	    CurveDivisor.deg k (thetaCoordinateSndDivisor (C := C) pi m) =
   174	      (m : Int) * windowδ pi := by
   175	  rw [thetaCoordinateSndDivisor, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_sub' k,
   176	    Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_nsmul' k, deg_fiberWeilDivisor_windowδ,
   177	    deg_divOf k, sub_zero]

   179	private theorem thetaCoordinate_window_h1 (g m : Nat) (hm : windowS_choice pi hpi g ≤ m) :
   180	    (Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.divisorSheaf k (m • F)) 1) ∧
   181	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
   182	        (C.left.divisorSheaf k (thetaCoordinateSndDivisor (C := C) pi m)) 1) ∧
   183	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
   184	        (C.left.divisorSheaf k ((m • F) ⊓
   185	          thetaCoordinateSndDivisor (C := C) pi m)) 1) ∧
   186	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
   187	        (C.left.divisorSheaf k ((m • F) ⊔
   188	          thetaCoordinateSndDivisor (C := C) pi m)) 1)) := by
   189	  have hδ : 0 ≤ windowδ pi := windowδ_nonneg pi
   190	  have hS : windowBound pi hpi + 2 * (g : Int) ≤
   191	      ((windowS_choice pi hpi g : Int) - 1) * windowδ pi :=
   192	    windowS_spec pi hpi g
   193	  have hm' : (windowS_choice pi hpi g : Int) ≤ (m : Int) := by
   194	    exact_mod_cast hm
   195	  have hb0 : windowBound pi hpi ≤ (m : Int) * windowδ pi := by
   196	    have hs0 : (windowS_choice pi hpi g : Int) * windowδ pi ≤
   197	        (m : Int) * windowδ pi := by
   198	      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hm' hδ
   199	    have := windowBound_le_S_mul pi hpi g
   200	    linarith
   201	  have hb1 : windowBound pi hpi ≤
   202	      CurveDivisor.deg k (thetaCoordinateSndDivisor (C := C) pi m) := by
   203	    rw [thetaCoordinateSndDivisor_deg]
   204	    exact hb0
   205	  have hsupdeg : CurveDivisor.deg k ((m • F) ⊔
   206	      thetaCoordinateSndDivisor (C := C) pi m) =
   207	      ((1 + m : Nat) : Int) * windowδ pi := by
   208	    rw [thetaCoordinate_sup, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_nsmul' k,
   209	      deg_fiberWeilDivisor_windowδ]
   210	  have hinfdeg : CurveDivisor.deg k ((m • F) ⊓
   211	      thetaCoordinateSndDivisor (C := C) pi m) =
   212	      ((m : Int) - 1) * windowδ pi := by
   213	    have hbal := Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_inf_add_deg_sup k (m • F)
   214	      (thetaCoordinateSndDivisor (C := C) pi m)
   215	    rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_nsmul' k, deg_fiberWeilDivisor_windowδ,
   216	      thetaCoordinateSndDivisor_deg, hsupdeg] at hbal
   217	    push_cast at hbal ⊢
   218	    nlinarith [hbal]
   219	  have hbinf : windowBound pi hpi ≤
   220	      CurveDivisor.deg k ((m • F) ⊓
   221	        thetaCoordinateSndDivisor (C := C) pi m) := by
   222	    rw [hinfdeg]
   223	    have hm1 : ((windowS_choice pi hpi g : Int) - 1) * windowδ pi ≤
   224	        ((m : Int) - 1) * windowδ pi := by
   225	      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (by linarith [hm']) hδ
   226	    linarith
   227	  have hbsup : windowBound pi hpi ≤
   228	      CurveDivisor.deg k ((m • F) ⊔ thetaCoordinateSndDivisor (C := C) pi m) := by
   229	    rw [hsupdeg]
   230	    have hmono : (m : Int) * windowδ pi ≤
   231	        ((1 + m : Nat) : Int) * windowδ pi := by
   232	      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (by omega) hδ
   233	    linarith
   234	  exact ⟨(by
   235	      apply windowBound_spec pi hpi _
   236	      rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_nsmul' k, deg_fiberWeilDivisor_windowδ]
   237	      exact hb0),
   238	    windowBound_spec pi hpi _ hb1,
   239	    windowBound_spec pi hpi _ hbinf,
   240	    windowBound_spec pi hpi _ hbsup⟩

   242	/-! ## The field-window span and elementwise recurrence -/
   243	
   244	set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000 in
   245	-- Rewriting both principal-divisor images and the dependent lattice supremum is expensive.
   246	theorem thetaCoordinate_window_span (g m : Nat)
   247	    (hm : windowS_choice pi hpi g ≤ m) :
   248	    Submodule.map (Scheme.mulLinear k (1 : C.left.functionField))
   249	        (divisorSections k (m • F) ⊤) ⊔
   250	      Submodule.map (Scheme.mulLinear k
   251	        ((u⁻¹ : C.left.functionFieldˣ) : C.left.functionField))
   252	        (divisorSections k (m • F) ⊤) =
   253	      divisorSections k ((1 + m) • F) ⊤ := by
   254	  have hwin := thetaCoordinate_window_h1 (C := C) pi hpi g m hm
   255	  have hfst := map_mulLinear_divisorSections_top k (f := (1 : C.left.functionField))
   256	    one_ne_zero (m • F)
   257	  have hsnd := map_mulLinear_divisorSections_top k
   258	    (f := ((u⁻¹ : C.left.functionFieldˣ) : C.left.functionField))
   259	    (Units.ne_zero (u⁻¹)) (m • F)
   260	  have hmk1 : Units.mk0 (1 : C.left.functionField) one_ne_zero = 1 :=
   261	    Units.ext rfl
   262	  have hmk : Units.mk0 ((u⁻¹ : C.left.functionFieldˣ) : C.left.functionField)
   263	      (Units.ne_zero (u⁻¹)) = u⁻¹ := Units.ext rfl
   264	  rw [hfst, hsnd, hmk1, Scheme.divOf_one, sub_zero, hmk]
   265	  calc
   266	    divisorSections k (m • F) ⊤ ⊔
   267	        divisorSections k (thetaCoordinateSndDivisor (C := C) pi m) ⊤ =
   268	      divisorSections k ((m • F) ⊔
   269	        thetaCoordinateSndDivisor (C := C) pi m) ⊤ :=
   270	      divisorSections_sup k (m • F)
   271	        (thetaCoordinateSndDivisor (C := C) pi m)
   272	        hwin.1 hwin.2.1 hwin.2.2.1 hwin.2.2.2
   273	    _ = divisorSections k ((1 + m) • F) ⊤ := by
   274	      rw [thetaCoordinate_sup]
   275	
   276	theorem exists_thetaCoordinate_decomposition (g m : Nat)
   277	    (hm : windowS_choice pi hpi g ≤ m) (h : H(1 + m)) :
   278	    ∃ z₀ z₁ : H m,
   279	      h = thetaWindowMul (C := C) (pi := pi) 1 m
   280	          (thetaCoordinateFstOne (C := C) pi hpi) z₀ +
   281	        thetaWindowMul (C := C) (pi := pi) 1 m
   282	          (thetaCoordinateSndOne (C := C) pi hpi) z₁ := by
   283	  have hspan := thetaCoordinate_window_span (C := C) pi hpi g m hm
   284	  have hh : (h : C.left.functionField) ∈
   285	      Submodule.map (Scheme.mulLinear k (1 : C.left.functionField))
   286	          (divisorSections k (m • F) ⊤) ⊔
   287	        Submodule.map (Scheme.mulLinear k
   288	          ((u⁻¹ : C.left.functionFieldˣ) : C.left.functionField))
   289	          (divisorSections k (m • F) ⊤) := by
   290	    rw [hspan]
   291	    exact h.property
   292	  obtain ⟨a, ha, b, hb, hab⟩ := Submodule.mem_sup.mp hh
   293	  rcases ha with ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩
   294	  rcases hb with ⟨b, hb, rfl⟩
   295	  refine ⟨⟨a, ha⟩, ⟨b, hb⟩, ?_⟩
   296	  apply Subtype.ext
   297	  rw [Submodule.coe_add, thetaWindowMul_coe, thetaWindowMul_coe,
   298	    thetaCoordinateFstOne_coe, thetaCoordinateSndOne_coe, one_mul]
   299	  simpa only [Scheme.mulLinear_apply, one_mul] using hab.symm

   303	/-- Componentwise multiplication of field theta pairs. -/
   304	noncomputable def thetaSectionPairMul (a b : Nat)
   305	    (x : ↥(twistSubmodule k (fiberChart₀ pi) (fiberChart₁ pi)
   306	      (thetaUnit pi ^ a) ⊤))
   307	    (y : ↥(twistSubmodule k (fiberChart₀ pi) (fiberChart₁ pi)
   308	      (thetaUnit pi ^ b) ⊤)) :
   309	    ↥(twistSubmodule k (fiberChart₀ pi) (fiberChart₁ pi)
   310	      (thetaUnit pi ^ (a + b)) ⊤) := by
   311	  refine ⟨(x.1.1 * y.1.1, x.1.2 * y.1.2), ?_⟩
   312	  rw [mem_twistSubmodule_iff]
   313	  have hx := (mem_twistSubmodule_iff k (fiberChart₀ pi) (fiberChart₁ pi)
   314	    (thetaUnit pi ^ a) x.1).mp x.2
   315	  have hy := (mem_twistSubmodule_iff k (fiberChart₀ pi) (fiberChart₁ pi)
   316	    (thetaUnit pi ^ b) y.1).mp y.2
   317	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, pow_add, Units.val_mul, map_mul, hx, hy]
   318	  ring
   319	
   320	theorem thetaSectionPair_thetaWindowMul (p q : Nat)
   321	    (a : ↥(divisorSections k (p • F) ⊤))
   322	    (m : ↥(divisorSections k (q • F) ⊤)) :
   323	    thetaSectionPair C pi (p + q)
   324	        (thetaWindowMul (C := C) (pi := pi) p q a m) =
   325	      thetaSectionPairMul (C := C) pi p q
   326	        (thetaSectionPair C pi p a) (thetaSectionPair C pi q m) := by
   327	  apply Subtype.ext
   328	  apply Prod.ext
   329	  · simpa [thetaSectionPairMul] using
   330	      (thetaSectionPair_thetaWindowMul_fst C pi p q a m)
   331	  · simpa [thetaSectionPairMul] using
   332	      (thetaSectionPair_thetaWindowMul_snd C pi p q a m)
   333	
   334	@[simp]
   335	theorem thetaSectionPair_add (n : Nat)
   336	    (a b : ↥(divisorSections k (n • F) ⊤)) :
   337	    thetaSectionPair C pi n (a + b) =
   338	      thetaSectionPair C pi n a + thetaSectionPair C pi n b := by
   339	  simp [thetaSectionPair]
   340	
   341	theorem exists_thetaSectionPair_coordinate_decomposition (g m : Nat)
   342	    (hm : windowS_choice pi hpi g ≤ m) (h : H(1 + m)) :
   343	    ∃ z₀ z₁ : H m,
   344	      thetaSectionPair C pi (1 + m) h =
   345	        thetaSectionPairMul (C := C) pi 1 m
   346	          (thetaSectionPair C pi 1 (thetaCoordinateFstOne (C := C) pi hpi))
   347	          (thetaSectionPair C pi m z₀) +
   348	        thetaSectionPairMul (C := C) pi 1 m
   349	          (thetaSectionPair C pi 1 (thetaCoordinateSndOne (C := C) pi hpi))
   350	          (thetaSectionPair C pi m z₁) := by
   351	  obtain ⟨z₀, z₁, hz⟩ := exists_thetaCoordinate_decomposition
   352	    (C := C) pi hpi g m hm h
   353	  refine ⟨z₀, z₁, ?_⟩
   354	  rw [hz, thetaSectionPair_add,
   355	    thetaSectionPair_thetaWindowMul, thetaSectionPair_thetaWindowMul]

    11	# Pure high-window multiplication spans
    12	
    13	Write `F = fiberWeilDivisor pi` and `S = windowS_choice pi hpi g`.  The
    14	two-coordinate recurrence gives
    15	
    16	`H^0((m+1)F) = H^0(mF) + u^-1 H^0(mF)`
    17	
    18	for `m >= S`.  Iterating this recurrence shows that every section in
    19	`H^0((q+m)F)` is a sum of products of a section in `H^0(qF)` and a section in
    20	`H^0(mF)`.  In particular, multiplication by the full `S`-window carries the
    21	pure arithmetic progression `S + n*S` onto its successor.
    22	
    23	This is the field-level normal-generation input for eventual closure of the
    24	recursive relation readings under arbitrary pinned-chart coefficients.  It
    25	makes no assertion over the nonreduced carve-chart ring.
    26	-/

    53	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsIntegral C.left]
    54	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    55	  [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    56	variable [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0)]
    57	  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)]

    60	/-- Every positive pure multiplier progression has vanishing `H^1`:
    61	`H^1(O((S + n*S)F)) = 0`. -/
    62	theorem window_embedding_pure_mul_iter (g n : Nat) :
    63	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.divisorSheaf k
    64	      ((windowS_choice pi hpi g + n * windowS_choice pi hpi g) •
    65	        fiberWeilDivisor pi)) 1) := by
    66	  refine windowBound_spec pi hpi _ ?_
    67	  rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_nsmul' k, deg_fiberWeilDivisor_windowδ]
    68	  have hS := windowBound_le_S_mul pi hpi g
    69	  have hS0 := windowS_mul_windowδ_nonneg pi hpi g
    70	  have hnS : 0 ≤ (n : Int) *
    71	      ((windowS_choice pi hpi g : Int) * windowδ pi) :=
    72	    mul_nonneg (Int.natCast_nonneg n) hS0
    73	  calc
    74	    windowBound pi hpi ≤
    75	        (windowS_choice pi hpi g : Int) * windowδ pi := hS
    76	    _ ≤ ((windowS_choice pi hpi g + n * windowS_choice pi hpi g : Nat) : Int) *
    77	        windowδ pi := by
    78	      push_cast
    79	      nlinarith

    81	/-- Relative-theta form of `window_embedding_pure_mul_iter`, supplying the
    82	window equivalence on the pure progression `S + n*S`. -/
    83	theorem relThetaPairH1_windowS_add_mulS (g n : Nat) :
    84	    Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k pi (relThetaCocycle C k pi
    85	      (windowS_choice pi hpi g + n * windowS_choice pi hpi g))).H1 :=

## Why I Stopped

The remaining statement is not merely technical. For every residue field and every high-window multiplication map, one must prove

```text
ker(multiplication) = range(Koszul boundary).
```

Only `range ⊆ ker` and multiplication surjectivity are currently proved. The missing reverse inclusion is precisely a relative Gotzmann/first-syzygy theorem, equivalently the unproved finrank lower bound at [DivSchemeHighWindowKoszul.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivSchemeHighWindowKoszul.lean:296).

Choosing the actual global kernel does not bypass this: [DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy.lean:254) proves that its fibre-base-change law is equivalent to the desired quotient flatness, so that argument would be circular.

The old Jacobian flattening theorem changes the base to locally closed rank strata and its Quot endpoint is still sorry-backed. The redesign theorem proves flatness only for the `RZ`-linear reading range, not the larger chart ideal. Neither is a drop-in completion.

Therefore representability is not yet fully formalized. The next substantive task is proving that relative first-syzygy rank estimate, or deliberately porting the full flattening-stratification route.

    27	  DAT-0a's packaging shifts, only `windowBound`/`windowBound_spec` change.
    28	* `windowδ π : ℤ` — the twist degree `δ = classDeg (Θ) = deg F ≥ 1` (DAT-0b).
    29	* `windowS_choice π hπ g : ℕ` — the multiplier step `s`, least with `(s − 1)·δ ≥ b + 3g`
    30	  (strengthened from `2g` for the P-fib-N tower budget, I-0234; the historical `2g` fact
    31	  survives as `windowS_spec`).
    32	* `windowM_choice π hπ g : ℕ` — the embedding exponent `M`, least with
    33	  `M·δ ≥ b + 2g + (g + 2)·(s + 1)·δ`.
    34	
    35	Here `g : ℕ` is the genus supplied by the consumer (the ledger arithmetic never assumes
    36	`g = χ`-anything; the rank exports take `χ(𝒪_Y) = 1 − g` as a hypothesis, discharged by
    37	the consumer's curve).
    38	
    39	## The windows (each an `H¹ = 0`, i.e. `Subsingleton (HModule (𝒪(…)) 1)`, via DAT-0a)
    40	
    41	Writing `F := fiberWeilDivisor π` (`deg F = δ`, `F ≥ 0`) and `P` any divisor with
    42	`deg P = δ` (the pole fibre of §1.1), for `deg D ≤ 2g` and `0 ≤ j ≤ g + 1`:
    43	
    44	* embedding windows `window_embedding{,_shift,_mult}`: `𝒪(A·F)` for `A ∈ {M, M+s, s}`;
    45	* normalization windows `window_normalization{,_shift}`: `𝒪(A·F − D)`;
    46	* lane windows `window_lane{,_shift}`: `𝒪(A·F − D − j·P)`;
    47	* the multiplier lane window `window_mult_lane`: `𝒪(s·F − D − P)` — F3's
    48	  `A_P`-surjectivity budget `(s − 1)·δ ≥ b + 2g` spent.
    49	
    50	All are proved from `windowBound_spec` (DAT-0a) applied to the degree of the divisor,
    51	whose lower bound `≥ b` is the arithmetic of `windowM_spec`/`windowS_spec`.
    52	
    53	## The rank values (rank anchor, `FLVClass.lean`)
    54	
    55	`rank_embedding{,_shift,_mult}` give `h⁰(𝒪(A·F)) = A·δ + χ(𝒪_Y)`, and the `…_of_genus`
    56	variants rewrite `χ(𝒪_Y) = 1 − g` to `r_A = A·δ + 1 − g` (§2.1). The lane dimensions of
    57	F2's graded pieces are `rank_normalization{,_shift}` and `rank_lane{,_shift}`:
    58	`h⁰ = A·δ − deg D − j·δ + χ(𝒪_Y)`.
    59	-/

    71	/-! ## Degree arithmetic helpers -/
    72	
    73	section DegHelpers
    74	
    75	variable {K : Type u} [CommRing K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
    76	  [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    77	
    78	/-- Degree of a natural multiple: `deg (n • D) = n · deg D`. -/
    79	private lemma deg_nsmul (n : ℕ) (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
    80	    CurveDivisor.deg K (n • D) = n * CurveDivisor.deg K D := by
    81	  induction n with
    82	  | zero => rw [zero_nsmul, CurveDivisor.deg_zero, Nat.cast_zero, zero_mul]
    83	  | succ n ih => rw [succ_nsmul, CurveDivisor.deg_add, ih]; push_cast; ring
    84	
    85	/-- Degree of a difference: `deg (A − B) = deg A − deg B`. -/
    86	private lemma deg_sub (A B : X.CurveDivisor) :
    87	    CurveDivisor.deg K (A - B) = CurveDivisor.deg K A - CurveDivisor.deg K B := by
    88	  rw [sub_eq_add_neg, CurveDivisor.deg_add, CurveDivisor.deg_neg, sub_eq_add_neg]
    89	
    90	end DegHelpers
    91	
    92	section Ledger
    93	
    94	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
    95	  [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    96	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    97	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    98	  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    99	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
   100	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
   101	  (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
   102	  (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap K = Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
   103	
   104	/-! ## The uniform vanishing bound `b` (DAT-0a, fixed choice) -/
   105	
   106	/-- **The DAT-0a bound `b`, fixed.** A `Classical.choose` of the existential
   107	`exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1`. This is the ledger's single
   108	contact point with DAT-0a (worksheet risk 7). -/
   109	noncomputable def windowBound : ℤ :=
   110	  (exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1 π hπ).choose
   111	
   112	/-- **The defining property of `b`**: every Weil divisor of degree `≥ b` has vanishing
   113	`H¹`. This is the only window fact all the specific windows below route through. -/
   114	theorem windowBound_spec (D : Y.CurveDivisor)
   115	    (hD : windowBound π hπ ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K D) :
   116	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K D) 1) :=
   117	  (exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1 π hπ).choose_spec D hD
   118	
   119	/-! ## The twist degree `δ` (DAT-0b) -/
   120	
   121	/-- **The twist degree `δ = classDeg Θ = deg F ≥ 1`.** -/
   122	noncomputable def windowδ : ℤ := classDeg K (fiberTwist π 1)
   123	
   124	/-- `1 ≤ δ` (DAT-0b, `one_le_classDeg_fiberTwist_one`). -/
   125	theorem one_le_windowδ : 1 ≤ windowδ π := one_le_classDeg_fiberTwist_one π
   126	
   127	/-- `0 ≤ δ`. -/
   128	theorem windowδ_nonneg : 0 ≤ windowδ π := le_trans zero_le_one (one_le_windowδ π)
   129	
   130	omit [IsFinite π] in
   131	/-- The fiber Weil divisor has degree `δ`: `deg F = δ` (DAT-0b,
   132	`classDeg_fiberTwist_one`). -/
   133	theorem deg_fiberWeilDivisor_windowδ :
   134	    CurveDivisor.deg K (fiberWeilDivisor π) = windowδ π :=
   135	  (classDeg_fiberTwist_one π).symm
   136	
   137	/-! ## The multiplier step `s` and the embedding exponent `M` -/
   138	
   139	private theorem windowS_exists (g : ℕ) :
   140	    ∃ s : ℕ, windowBound π hπ + 3 * (g : ℤ) ≤ ((s : ℤ) - 1) * windowδ π := by
   141	  set T : ℤ := windowBound π hπ + 3 * (g : ℤ) with hT
   142	  refine ⟨T.toNat + 1, ?_⟩
   143	  have hδ : 1 ≤ windowδ π := one_le_windowδ π
   144	  have h1 : ((T.toNat : ℤ)) ≤ (T.toNat : ℤ) * windowδ π :=
   145	    le_mul_of_one_le_right (Int.natCast_nonneg _) hδ
   146	  have h2 : T ≤ (T.toNat : ℤ) := Int.self_le_toNat T
   147	  have h3 : (((T.toNat + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) - 1) = (T.toNat : ℤ) := by push_cast; ring
   148	  rw [h3]; linarith
   149	
   150	/-- **The multiplier step `s`** — least `s` with `(s − 1)·δ ≥ b + 3g` (worksheet §2.1,
   151	budget strengthened `2g → 3g` for the P-fib-N tower discharge at residue fields,
   152	I-0234). Used by F3 (graded surjectivity of `H_s` onto the `P`-level algebra). -/
   153	noncomputable def windowS_choice (g : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.find (windowS_exists π hπ g)
   154	
   155	/-- **The strengthened defining inequality of `s`**: `(s − 1)·δ ≥ b + 3g` — the
   156	P-fib-N tower budget `hβS` at `κ(p)` (I-0234). -/
   157	theorem windowS_spec_three (g : ℕ) :
   158	    windowBound π hπ + 3 * (g : ℤ) ≤ ((windowS_choice π hπ g : ℤ) - 1) * windowδ π :=
   159	  Nat.find_spec (windowS_exists π hπ g)
   160	
   161	/-- **The original defining inequality of `s`**: `(s − 1)·δ ≥ b + 2g` — kept in its
   162	historical shape so every pre-I-0234 consumer is byte-compatible; strictly weaker than
   163	`windowS_spec_three`. F3's `A_P`-surjectivity window. -/
   164	theorem windowS_spec (g : ℕ) :
   165	    windowBound π hπ + 2 * (g : ℤ) ≤ ((windowS_choice π hπ g : ℤ) - 1) * windowδ π := by
   166	  have h := windowS_spec_three π hπ g
   167	  have hg : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (g : ℤ) := Int.natCast_nonneg _
   168	  linarith
   169	
   170	private theorem windowM_exists (g : ℕ) :
   171	    ∃ M : ℕ, windowBound π hπ + 2 * (g : ℤ)
   172	        + ((g : ℤ) + 2) * ((windowS_choice π hπ g : ℤ) + 1) * windowδ π
   173	      ≤ (M : ℤ) * windowδ π := by
   174	  set U : ℤ := windowBound π hπ + 2 * (g : ℤ)
   175	      + ((g : ℤ) + 2) * ((windowS_choice π hπ g : ℤ) + 1) * windowδ π with hU
   176	  refine ⟨U.toNat, ?_⟩
   177	  have hδ : 1 ≤ windowδ π := one_le_windowδ π
   178	  have h1 : ((U.toNat : ℤ)) ≤ (U.toNat : ℤ) * windowδ π :=
   179	    le_mul_of_one_le_right (Int.natCast_nonneg _) hδ
   180	  have h2 : U ≤ (U.toNat : ℤ) := Int.self_le_toNat U
   181	  linarith
   182	
   183	/-- **The embedding exponent `M`** — least `M` with `M·δ ≥ b + 2g + (g + 2)·(s + 1)·δ`
   184	(worksheet §2.1). Chosen so every embedding/normalization/lane window down to depth
   185	`g + 1` in `P`-steps stays `≥ b`. -/
   186	noncomputable def windowM_choice (g : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.find (windowM_exists π hπ g)
   187	
   188	/-- **The defining inequality of `M`**: `M·δ ≥ b + 2g + (g + 2)·(s + 1)·δ`. -/
   189	theorem windowM_spec (g : ℕ) :
   190	    windowBound π hπ + 2 * (g : ℤ)
   191	        + ((g : ℤ) + 2) * ((windowS_choice π hπ g : ℤ) + 1) * windowδ π
   192	      ≤ (windowM_choice π hπ g : ℤ) * windowδ π :=
   193	  Nat.find_spec (windowM_exists π hπ g)
   194	
   195	/-! ## Derived degree lower bounds -/
   196	
   197	/-- **The embedding bound**: `b ≤ M·δ`. -/
   198	theorem windowBound_le_M_mul (g : ℕ) :
   199	    windowBound π hπ ≤ (windowM_choice π hπ g : ℤ) * windowδ π := by
   200	  have hspec := windowM_spec π hπ g
   201	  have hnn : 0 ≤ ((g : ℤ) + 2) * ((windowS_choice π hπ g : ℤ) + 1) * windowδ π :=
   202	    mul_nonneg (mul_nonneg (by positivity) (by positivity)) (windowδ_nonneg π)
   203	  linarith
   204	
   205	/-- **The embedding bound at `s`**: `b ≤ s·δ`. -/
   206	theorem windowBound_le_S_mul (g : ℕ) :
   207	    windowBound π hπ ≤ (windowS_choice π hπ g : ℤ) * windowδ π := by
   208	  have hspec := windowS_spec π hπ g
   209	  have hδ : 0 ≤ windowδ π := windowδ_nonneg π
   210	  have hg : (0 : ℤ) ≤ 2 * (g : ℤ) := by positivity
   211	  -- `(s − 1)·δ ≥ b + 2g ≥ b`, and `s·δ = (s−1)·δ + δ ≥ (s−1)·δ`
   212	  nlinarith [hspec, hδ, hg]
   213	
   214	/-- **The normalization bound**: `b ≤ M·δ − 2g`. -/
   215	theorem windowBound_le_M_norm (g : ℕ) :
   216	    windowBound π hπ ≤ (windowM_choice π hπ g : ℤ) * windowδ π - 2 * (g : ℤ) := by
   217	  have hspec := windowM_spec π hπ g
   218	  have hnn : 0 ≤ ((g : ℤ) + 2) * ((windowS_choice π hπ g : ℤ) + 1) * windowδ π :=
   219	    mul_nonneg (mul_nonneg (by positivity) (by positivity)) (windowδ_nonneg π)
   220	  linarith
   221	
   222	/-- **The lane bound**: `b ≤ M·δ − 2g − (g + 1)·δ`. Every `M`-lane window at depth
   223	`≤ g + 1` in `P`-steps and effective slack `deg D ≤ 2g` sits above it. -/
   224	theorem windowBound_le_M_lane (g : ℕ) :
   225	    windowBound π hπ
   226	      ≤ (windowM_choice π hπ g : ℤ) * windowδ π - 2 * (g : ℤ)
   227	          - ((g : ℤ) + 1) * windowδ π := by
   228	  have hspec := windowM_spec π hπ g
   229	  have hδ : 0 ≤ windowδ π := windowδ_nonneg π
   230	  have hs : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (windowS_choice π hπ g : ℤ) := Int.natCast_nonneg _
   231	  have hg : (0 : ℤ) ≤ (g : ℤ) := Int.natCast_nonneg _
   232	  -- `(g + 2)·(s + 1) − (g + 1) ≥ 1 ≥ 0`, so `(g+2)(s+1)δ ≥ (g+1)δ`
   233	  have hcoeff : ((g : ℤ) + 1) ≤ ((g : ℤ) + 2) * ((windowS_choice π hπ g : ℤ) + 1) := by
   234	    nlinarith [hs, hg]
   235	  have hmul : ((g : ℤ) + 1) * windowδ π
   236	      ≤ ((g : ℤ) + 2) * ((windowS_choice π hπ g : ℤ) + 1) * windowδ π :=
   237	    mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hcoeff hδ
   238	  linarith
   239	
   240	/-- The shift slack: `0 ≤ s·δ` — the `M ↦ M + s` window shifts only raise degrees. -/
   241	theorem windowS_mul_windowδ_nonneg (g : ℕ) :
   242	    0 ≤ (windowS_choice π hπ g : ℤ) * windowδ π :=
   243	  mul_nonneg (Int.natCast_nonneg _) (windowδ_nonneg π)
   244	
   245	/-! ## The windows: `H¹ = 0` at every twist the P-fib route visits (§3.3)
   246	
   247	Every lemma is `windowBound_spec` (DAT-0a) plus ledger arithmetic; no consumer restates
   248	a degree bound. -/
   249	
   250	/-- **The embedding window**: `H¹(𝒪(M·F)) = 0`. The window carrying the first
   251	Grassmannian factor `H_M`. -/
   252	theorem window_embedding (g : ℕ) :
   253	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
   254	      (Y.divisorSheaf K (windowM_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π)) 1) := by
   255	  refine windowBound_spec π hπ _ ?_
   256	  rw [deg_nsmul, deg_fiberWeilDivisor_windowδ]
   257	  exact windowBound_le_M_mul π hπ g
   258	
   259	/-- **The shifted embedding window**: `H¹(𝒪((M+s)·F)) = 0`. The window carrying the
   260	second Grassmannian factor `H_{M+s}`. -/
   261	theorem window_embedding_shift (g : ℕ) :
   262	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K
   263	      ((windowM_choice π hπ g + windowS_choice π hπ g) • fiberWeilDivisor π)) 1) := by
   264	  refine windowBound_spec π hπ _ ?_
   265	  rw [deg_nsmul, deg_fiberWeilDivisor_windowδ]
   266	  have hM := windowBound_le_M_mul π hπ g
   267	  have hs := windowS_mul_windowδ_nonneg π hπ g
   268	  push_cast
   269	  linarith
   270	
   271	/-- **The multiplier window**: `H¹(𝒪(s·F)) = 0`. The window carrying the multiplier
   272	space `H_s` of the carve `(♦)`. -/
   273	theorem window_embedding_mult (g : ℕ) :
   274	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
   275	      (Y.divisorSheaf K (windowS_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π)) 1) := by
   276	  refine windowBound_spec π hπ _ ?_
   277	  rw [deg_nsmul, deg_fiberWeilDivisor_windowδ]
   278	  exact windowBound_le_S_mul π hπ g
   279	
   280	/-- **The normalization window**: `H¹(𝒪(M·F − D)) = 0` for every divisor of degree
   281	`≤ 2g` (in particular the F1 base divisor, whose degree the section bound caps at `2g`).
   282	-/
   283	theorem window_normalization (g : ℕ) (D : Y.CurveDivisor)
   284	    (hD : CurveDivisor.deg K D ≤ 2 * (g : ℤ)) :
   285	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K
   286	      (windowM_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π - D)) 1) := by
   287	  refine windowBound_spec π hπ _ ?_
   288	  rw [deg_sub, deg_nsmul, deg_fiberWeilDivisor_windowδ]
   289	  have hM := windowBound_le_M_norm π hπ g
   290	  linarith
   291	
   292	/-- **The shifted normalization window**: `H¹(𝒪((M+s)·F − D)) = 0` for `deg D ≤ 2g`. -/
   293	theorem window_normalization_shift (g : ℕ) (D : Y.CurveDivisor)
   294	    (hD : CurveDivisor.deg K D ≤ 2 * (g : ℤ)) :
   295	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K
   296	      ((windowM_choice π hπ g + windowS_choice π hπ g) • fiberWeilDivisor π - D)) 1) := by
   297	  refine windowBound_spec π hπ _ ?_
   298	  rw [deg_sub, deg_nsmul, deg_fiberWeilDivisor_windowδ]
   299	  have hM := windowBound_le_M_norm π hπ g
   300	  have hs := windowS_mul_windowδ_nonneg π hπ g

    10	/-!
    11	# Persistence at every high divisor-scheme window
    12	
    13	The two Grassmannian windows recover an effective degree-`g` divisor `D` on every
    14	field fibre.  The same multiplication argument is not confined to those first two
    15	windows: after replacing `N` by `N + n * S`, the degree budgets only improve.  Thus
    16	the full `S`-window carries `H^0(O(N + n*S - D))` onto the next stage for every `n`.
    17	
    18	This is the field-level persistence input for an eventual relative saturation or
    19	direct-limit construction.  It does not itself construct the relative high-window
    20	modules over the carve-chart ring.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	set_option autoImplicit false
    24	
    25	universe u
    26	
    27	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace
    28	
    29	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    30	
    31	open Scheme Grassmannian
    32	
    33	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    34	  Scheme.functionFieldOverModule
    35	
    36	section Pack
    37	
    38	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
    39	  [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    40	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    41	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    42	  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    43	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
    44	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
    45	
    46	/-- Multiplication persistence is uniform in the high-window index.  The hypotheses
    47	are exactly the abstract P-fib window pack at `N` and `S`; at `N + n • S` all degree
    48	and normalization inequalities follow from the original ones. -/
    49	theorem mulSpan_divisorSections_highWindow_of_pack
    50	    (g : ℕ) (hO : Sheaf.h0 (Y.moduleKSheaf K) = 1)
    51	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
    52	    (N S : Y.CurveDivisor) (β : ℤ)
    53	    (hvan : ∀ W : Y.CurveDivisor, β ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K W →
    54	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1))
    55	    (hNdeg : 2 * (g : ℤ) ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K N)
    56	    (hSdeg : 2 * (g : ℤ) ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K S)
    57	    (hβS : β + 2 * (g : ℤ) ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K S)
    58	    (hβN : β + 2 * (g : ℤ) + CurveDivisor.deg K S ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K N)
    59	    (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (hD0 : 0 ≤ D)
    60	    (hDdeg : CurveDivisor.deg K D = (g : ℤ)) (n : ℕ) :
    61	    Scheme.mulSpan K (divisorSections K S ⊤)
    62	        (divisorSections K (N + n • S - D) ⊤) =
    63	      divisorSections K (N + (n + 1) • S - D) ⊤ := by
    64	  classical
    65	  let Nn : Y.CurveDivisor := N + n • S
    66	  have hSdeg0 : 0 ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K S := by omega
    67	  have hNndeg : CurveDivisor.deg K Nn =
    68	      CurveDivisor.deg K N + (n : ℤ) * CurveDivisor.deg K S := by
    69	    dsimp [Nn]
    70	    rw [CurveDivisor.deg_add, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_nsmul']
    71	  have hβNn : β + 2 * (g : ℤ) + CurveDivisor.deg K S ≤
    72	      CurveDivisor.deg K Nn := by
    73	    rw [hNndeg]
    74	    have hn : 0 ≤ (n : ℤ) * CurveDivisor.deg K S :=
    75	      mul_nonneg (Int.natCast_nonneg n) hSdeg0
    76	    omega
    77	  have hNnDeg : 2 * (g : ℤ) ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K Nn := by
    78	    rw [hNndeg]
    79	    have hn : 0 ≤ (n : ℤ) * CurveDivisor.deg K S :=
    80	      mul_nonneg (Int.natCast_nonneg n) hSdeg0
    81	    omega
    82	  have hNnNorm : ∀ D' : Y.CurveDivisor,
    83	      CurveDivisor.deg K D' ≤ 2 * (g : ℤ) →
    84	        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (Nn - D')) 1) := by
    85	    intro D' hD'
    86	    apply hvan
    87	    rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_sub' K, hNndeg]
    88	    have hn : 0 ≤ (n : ℤ) * CurveDivisor.deg K S :=
    89	      mul_nonneg (Int.natCast_nonneg n) hSdeg0
    90	    omega
    91	  let T : Submodule K Y.functionField := divisorSections K (Nn - D) ⊤

text: A concrete route is emerging from the window arithmetic. The huge `M` budget is strong enough for a basepoint-free pencil argument: use `1` and `u^{-S}` inside the multiplier window, reduce arbitrary full-window relations to that pencil, and spend one `H¹(A-2S)=0` vanishing to lift coefficients. This would prove the required first Koszul exactness without importing general Gotzmann theory. I’m checking that the existing divisor-section lattice API supports the two pencil lemmas cleanly.

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeHighWindowPencil
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.SumIntersection

/-!
# A divisor-section pencil for high-window syzygies

Let `v` be a rational unit and let `B` be the preceding divisor window for a
current window `A`.  The two sections `1` and `v` give the required pencil when

* `B ⊔ (B - div(v)) = A`, which makes their products span `H^0(A)`; and
* `A ⊓ (A + div(v)) = B`, which identifies their two-term kernel.

The first assertion uses the sum-intersection dimension theorem and hence four
`H^1` vanishings.  The second is pure divisor-section lattice algebra.  The
final theorem feeds both statements into the finite-basis pencil reduction.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u v

open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open Scheme

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.functionFieldOverModule

variable {K : Type u} [Field K]
variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
  [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]

/-! ## Spanning by the two pencil sections -/

/-- If the two translated preceding divisors have supremum `A`, their section
spaces span the current window. -/
theorem exists_divisorSections_pencil_decomposition
    (A B : X.CurveDivisor) (w : X.functionFieldˣ)
    (hsup : B ⊔
        (B - Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) w) = A)
    (hB : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K B) 1))
    (hBw : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K
      (B - Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) w)) 1))
    (hinf : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K
      (B ⊓ (B - Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) w))) 1))
    (hsupH : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K
      (B ⊔ (B - Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) w))) 1))
    (x : divisorSections K A ⊤) :
    ∃ z : Fin 2 → divisorSections K B ⊤,
      (x : X.functionField) =
        (z 0 : X.functionField) + (w : X.functionField) * (z 1 : X.functionField) := by
  let D := Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) w
  have hmul : Submodule.map (Scheme.mulLinear K (w : X.functionField))
        (divisorSections K B ⊤) = divisorSections K (B - D) ⊤ := by
    rw [map_mulLinear_divisorSections_top K (Units.ne_zero w) B]
    have hmk : Units.mk0 (w : X.functionField) (Units.ne_zero w) = w := Units.ext rfl
    rw [hmk]
  have hsections : divisorSections K B ⊤ ⊔
      Submodule.map (Scheme.mulLinear K (w : X.functionField))
        (divisorSections K B ⊤) = divisorSections K A ⊤ := by
    rw [hmul, divisorSections_sup K B (B - D) hB hBw hinf hsupH, hsup]
  have hx : (x : X.functionField) ∈ divisorSections K B ⊤ ⊔
      Submodule.map (Scheme.mulLinear K (w : X.functionField))
        (divisorSections K B ⊤) := by
    rw [hsections]
    exact x.property
  obtain ⟨a, ha, b, hb, hab⟩ := Submodule.mem_sup.mp hx
  obtain ⟨z, hz, rfl⟩ := hb
  let z0 : divisorSections K B ⊤ := ⟨a, ha⟩
  let z1 : divisorSections K B ⊤ := ⟨z, hz⟩
  let z' : Fin 2 → divisorSections K B ⊤ := fun q => if q = 0 then z0 else z1
  refine ⟨z', ?_⟩
  simpa [z', z0, z1, Scheme.mulLinear_apply] using hab.symm

/-! ## The two-term kernel -/

omit [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)] in
/-- The relation kernel of the two sections `1,w` is generated by the
preceding window when that window is the indicated divisor intersection. -/
theorem exists_divisorSections_pencil_relation
    (A B : X.CurveDivisor) (w : X.functionFieldˣ)
    (hinf : A ⊓
        (A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) w) = B)
    (y : Fin 2 → divisorSections K A ⊤)
    (hy : (y 0 : X.functionField) +
      (w : X.functionField) * (y 1 : X.functionField) = 0) :
    ∃ z : divisorSections K B ⊤,
      (y 0 : X.functionField) = (w : X.functionField) * (z : X.functionField) ∧
      (y 1 : X.functionField) = -(z : X.functionField) := by
  let D := Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) w
  have hwyA : (w : X.functionField) * (y 1 : X.functionField) ∈
      divisorSections K A ⊤ := by
    have heq : (w : X.functionField) * (y 1 : X.functionField) =
        -(y 0 : X.functionField) := by
      linear_combination hy
    rw [heq]
    exact (divisorSections K A ⊤).neg_mem (y 0).property
  have hmap : Submodule.map (Scheme.mulLinear K (w : X.functionField))
      (divisorSections K (A + D) ⊤) = divisorSections K A ⊤ := by
    rw [map_mulLinear_divisorSections_top K (Units.ne_zero w)]
    have hmk : Units.mk0 (w : X.functionField) (Units.ne_zero w) = w := Units.ext rfl
    rw [hmk]
    change divisorSections K (A + D - D) ⊤ = divisorSections K A ⊤
    congr 2
    abel
  have hwyMap : (w : X.functionField) * (y 1 : X.functionField) ∈
      Submodule.map (Scheme.mulLinear K (w : X.functionField))
        (divisorSections K (A + D) ⊤) := by
    rw [hmap]
    exact hwyA
  obtain ⟨t, ht, htw⟩ := hwyMap

    change (w : X.functionField) * t =
      (w : X.functionField) * (y 1 : X.functionField) at htw
    exact mul_left_cancel₀ (Units.ne_zero w) htw
  have hyAD : (y 1 : X.functionField) ∈ divisorSections K (A + D) ⊤ := by
    rwa [hty] at ht
  have hyB : (y 1 : X.functionField) ∈ divisorSections K B ⊤ := by
    have hmem : (y 1 : X.functionField) ∈
        divisorSections K A ⊤ ⊓ divisorSections K (A + D) ⊤ :=
      Submodule.mem_inf.mpr ⟨(y 1).property, hyAD⟩
    rw [divisorSections_inf K A (A + D), hinf] at hmem
    exact hmem

    (divisorSections K B ⊤).neg_mem hyB⟩
  refine ⟨z, ?_, ?_⟩
  · change (y 0 : X.functionField) = (w : X.functionField) * -(y 1 : X.functionField)
    calc
      (y 0 : X.functionField) =
          -((w : X.functionField) * (y 1 : X.functionField)) :=
